content: The traditional emphasis on tertiary care hospitals is shifting towards initiatives that promote community engagement. The guidelines advocate for the integration of community and national efforts to bring about transformative changes in the education of health professionals. These guidelines aim to encourage educational and training institutions to enhance collaboration and planning between education, health, and other sectors. The World Health Organization (WHO) has launched an initiative to transform and scale up the education and training of health professionals. This initiative is a significant step towards reshaping the health workforce to better serve the needs and well-being of populations. The guidelines outline a vision for transforming health professional education and provide recommendations to produce graduates who are responsive to the health needs of the communities they serve. The guidelines specifically aim to: 1. Provide sound policy and technical guidance in pre-service education, particularly in countries facing shortages of doctors, nurses, midwives, and other health professionals. 2. Guide countries on integrating continuing professional development (CPD) into health professional education to ensure high-quality care, responsive health service delivery, and sustainable health systems. Country ownership is essential in determining priorities and setting policies across five identified domains: 1. Education and training institutions. 2. Accreditation and regulation. 3. Financing and sustainability. 4. Monitoring and evaluation. 5. Governance and planning. The recommendations include developing community-engaged curricula, equipping health professionals with skills to become competent clinical teachers, and preparing graduates to work in underserved areas. Greater alignment between educational institutions and healthcare systems is necessary to achieve transformative change and leadership in preparing future graduates. Transformative scaling up of health professional education involves sustainably expanding and reforming education to increase the quantity, quality, and relevance of health professionals. This process strengthens health systems and improves population health outcomes. The guidelines address complex issues in transforming health professional education by presenting key policy issues, summarizing evidence, and providing recommendations with implementation guidance. Key recommendations include: Designing continuous development programs for faculty to address evolving healthcare needs. Supporting mandatory faculty development programs through government and accrediting bodies. Expanding faculty by recruiting community-based clinicians and health workers as educators. Adapting curricula to meet the changing healthcare needs of communities. Using simulation methods in education, tailored to resource availability. Considering direct entry of graduates from relevant programs into professional studies. Implementing targeted admissions policies to increase diversity among students. Using streamlined educational pathways and ladder programs for advancing practicing health professionals. Introducing inter-professional education (IPE) in undergraduate and postgraduate programs. Establishing or strengthening accreditation systems for health professional education. Implementing CPD and in-service training relevant to evolving healthcare needs. The guidelines emphasize the importance of political commitment and leadership at the highest levels of government to drive reform. They advocate for national plans to produce and retain graduates, informed by labor market needs and aligned with national health plans. The guidelines also highlight the need for vibrant and sustainable educational institutions with dynamic curricula, supportive learning environments, and high-quality faculty. The WHO guidelines were developed using a rigorous evidence-informed process, including the synthesis of research, assessment of evidence quality, and consideration of resource use and values. The process was guided by a diverse group of experts and stakeholders, ensuring geographic and gender balance. The guidelines aim to provide practical strategies for transforming and scaling up health professional education globally, addressing workforce shortages, and improving health outcomes.
